headline: North-West conveyor failure is driving nearly the entire SLA drop.
body: The WH-07 conveyor failure on June 25 cut sortation capacity to 60%, and the spare part is still three weeks out [E5]. That single region accounts for essentially all of the SLA decline, while other regions are flat or improving. A prior East region incident with the same failure mode recovered in 12 days once overflow capacity was added, but that mitigation wasn't deployed here [E4]. A competing SLA-linked hypothesis, SwiftKart's new express launch, is plausible but unconfirmed and can't explain the July persistence pattern on its own.

actions.action: Activate pre-approved 3PL overflow for North-West lanes now
actions.expected_impact: Recover SLA to baseline in about 12 days, per precedent
actions.monitoring: Track North-West SLA daily until back above 90%

actions.expected_impact: Restores throughput while conveyor part is on backorder
actions.monitoring: Monitor daily throughput and picker headcount at WH-07

what_could_change: Confirmation that conveyor part arrival or overflow rollout timing shifts, or evidence SwiftKart's launch is pulling volume independent of the outage, would revise this.
caveats: The SwiftKart express-launch hypothesis is uncorroborated by internal data and should not be treated as a confirmed driver yet.
clarifying_question: Can we get confirmed ETA for the conveyor spare part and current 3PL overflow rollout status?
